title: Molecular Structure and Designed Materials
seo_title: Materials Chemistry Worksheets: Structure, Polymers and Solubility (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Communicate scientific and technical information about why the molecular-level structure is important in the functioning of designed materials.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on molecular structure and designed materials (NGSS HS-PS2-6): metals, ionic and network solids, polymers, solubility and choosing materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: How particles are arranged and bonded explains why a material conducts, stretches or dissolves.
body_html:
How to think about it

Structure at the particle level decides how a material behaves.

  • Metals: sea of electrons → conduct and bend. Ionic solids: hard, brittle, conduct when melted or dissolved. Network solids: very hard.
  • Polymers: long chains of monomers; chain shape and forces give stretch, strength or water resistance.
  • Like dissolves like: polar or ionic in water; nonpolar in nonpolar solvents.
Example

Why does graphite conduct but diamond does not?

Graphite has free electrons in its layers

Answer: free-moving electrons

Example

Will oil dissolve in water?

Oil nonpolar, water polar

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking graphite and diamond are different elements.
  • Thinking stirring makes oil dissolve in water.
  • Thinking all solids conduct electricity.

faq.q: Why does molecular structure matter for materials?
faq.a: The way atoms are bonded and arranged decides properties such as strength, conductivity, flexibility and solubility.
A very large molecule made by linking many small units called monomers, such as ethylene in polyethylene.

faq.q: What does like dissolves like mean?
faq.a: Polar and ionic substances dissolve in polar solvents such as water; nonpolar substances dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
